newsitem.title: UK: London gold tests key $379-$380 support area.
newsitem.headline: London gold tests key $379-$380 support area.

text.p: Gold fixed below the psychological $380 support on Monday for the first time in over a year after edging down in jittery early trading, traders said.
"There's a general concern in Europe that it's not over yet. There's been some selling around," a dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $379.30 an ounce, compared to $380.70 on Friday afternoon and a London close of $380.90/$381.40.
The fixing was a fresh low since September 6, 1995.
Below $380, the technical $379 support level was expected to come into play, analysts said. If that also crumbled, the rest of the precious metals were at risk of tumbling with gold.
Bearish market sentiment deepened on Friday after gold failed to manage a decent bounce following a brief dip to just under $380, dealers said.
"With the market as short as it is, it didn't do enough, and closed a bit weak," a dealer said.
However, the fact that the drop was coming at the month-end could spark some book-squaring and help boost prices.

The market generally ignored news that the International Monetary Fund had again left open a decision at a weekend meeting on whether to sell five million ounces of gold to help poor countries, dealers said.
"All the talk as been about IMF gold sales...but the impact will not be so dramatic, as i think the market would absorb up to five million ounces over time," a European analyst said.
The market was more attuned to downward-pointing technicals at the present time, dealers said.
Several analysts have said gold could easily target the $360 area, especially if price-sensitive Asian and Mideast consumers wait for lower prices before stepping up demand.
The 14-day RSI was at 27.75, indicating the market was technically oversold, however. European dealers would be carefully watching the reaction on New York's Comex market.
Silver was easier with gold at $4.87/$4.99, down five cents from Friday's London close. But so far its reaction to gold's dip was muted and it was nowhere near recent lows.
But analysts said a confirmed breach $379-$380 for gold would most likely drag the white metals lower, with silver targetting as low as $4.50.

Platinum was also easier at $383.75/$384.75, off $1.00, but it was comfortably esconsced in its $380-$390 range for now. Palladium was steady at $118.25/$119.25, although it was seen vulnerable to the downside, targetting the $112-$115 area.
